title: Lace bottom-up triangle shawl
subtitle: A fingering-weight triangle cast on at the full wingspan and decreased to a neck point with allover lace.
excerpt: A bottom-up triangular shawl in fingering-weight wool with an allover 6-stitch horseshoe lace pattern throughout the body. Cast on at the full 190 cm wingspan and decreased on every right-side row to a three-stitch point. About 380 g of fingering yarn. The horseshoe lace pattern is a classic Victorian lace stitch.
sourceNotes: The horseshoe lace pattern (k2tog, yo, k2, yo, ssk; 6 sts over 6 rows) is documented in Weldon's Practical Knitter, 5th series (1890), §Lace Stitches: Horseshoe Pattern. The bottom-up triangular construction appears in Weldon's Practical Knitter, 2nd series (1886), §Shawls.

knitting.gaugeText: 24 sts × 48 rows = 10 × 10 cm in stockinette on 3.75 mm needles, blocked.
knitting.gaugeInPatternStitch: 24 sts × 40 rows = 10 × 10 cm in horseshoe lace on 3.75 mm needles, blocked.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Wingspan 190 cm. Centre-back depth 90 cm. Blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A symmetrical 6-stitch lace motif: k2tog, yo, k2, yo, ssk. The two yarn-overs meet at the centre, creating an arch resembling a horseshoe. On a 6-row repeat, successive arches form a chain across the fabric.

content.text: A bottom-up triangular shawl in fingering-weight wool with an allover
horseshoe lace
pattern throughout, cast on at the full 190 cm wingspan and decreased to a three-stitch neck point. Wingspan 190 cm, centre-back depth 90 cm when blocked.

The bottom-up construction is ideal for the horseshoe pattern: the first rows are the longest, so the full lace repeat runs from the start and remains consistent as the shawl narrows. The decreases for the triangular shaping are placed at each edge of the spine on every RS row. Budget about 380 g (about 1,520 m / 1,660 yards) of fingering wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: About 380 g (1,520 m / 1,660 yards) of fingering-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, 120 cm or longer

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 1 for centre spine, several for lace repeat boundaries

items.name: Tapestry needle, scissors, blocking mat, pins

content.text: Gauge

24 stitches and 40 rows to 10 cm over horseshoe lace on 3.75 mm needles, blocked. The cast-on for a 190 cm wingspan at 24 stitches per 10 cm is approximately 456 stitches. If your blocked gauge reads 26 stitches per 10 cm, cast on 494 stitches (the nearest multiple of 6 that gives 190 cm at that gauge).
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast on
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 456 stitches (76 horseshoe repeats × 6 sts). Allow a tail of approximately (3.75 × 456) / 10 + 15 = 186 cm. Place a centre marker after stitch 228.
Set-up rows
Rows 1 to 4: k all sts.
Horseshoe lace decrease section

RS lace rows (every RS row is a decrease row): k1, ssk, work horseshoe lace pattern across body to 3 sts before centre, k2tog, k1, SM, k1, ssk, work horseshoe lace to last 3 sts, k2tog, k1. (4 sts decreased per RS row)
WS rows: k3, p to 3 sts before end, k3.

Horseshoe lace RS row (6 sts): k2tog, yo, k2, yo, ssk. The decreases and increases within each repeat balance (stitch count unchanged within the repeat); only the 4 edge/spine decreases reduce total count.
Continue until 3 stitches remain (approximately 113 RS decrease rows at gauge). Bind off the final 3 stitches using a standard bind-off.
Stitch count check-ins
After 60 RS rows: 456 - 240 = 216 stitches. Each wing holds about 107 stitches. The horseshoe arches should be clearly visible in the body.
After 100 RS rows: 456 - 400 = 56 stitches. The shawl narrows quickly at this point; the lace repeats shorten.
Common faults

Lace repeat count broken as shawl narrows: the 6-stitch horseshoe repeat no longer divides evenly into the remaining stitch count. Once fewer than 6 stitches remain in a wing section, work those stitches in plain garter rather than attempting a partial horseshoe.
Cast-on edge too tight to block to full 190 cm: cast on over two needles held together for an automatically looser cast-on edge.
Blocking
Soak 20 minutes in cool water, press out in towels. Pin the cast-on edge to the full 190 cm wingspan. Pin the neck point at the full 90 cm depth. The horseshoe arches open dramatically under pinning.
Care
Hand wash in cool water, lay flat to dry. Re-block when the horseshoe lace closes up after wearing.
What to try next

Work the same horseshoe pattern in lace-weight yarn on 2.75 mm needles for a much finer, more open shawl in the same construction. The same row count will produce a wingspan of approximately 140 cm at lace weight.
